get.description: Returns 200 while the process is serving. Touches no dependency.
Returns 200 when every dependency is reachable, 503 when one is not.

post.description: Accepts the registration and answers 202 whether or not the address is already registered. A 409 here would tell an anonymous caller who holds an account; the mailbox tells the real user what happened.

Spends the token from the verification mail exactly once and marks the address verified. The description says nothing about what separates 400 from 410 for a given token, because that is the caller's business only when they hold it.

post.summary: Ask for another email verification link
post.description: Answers 202 for any address that is a valid address. Whether a mail follows is not stated and cannot be inferred from the response: a distinct answer here would tell an anonymous caller which addresses hold a registered or confirmed account.

Exchanges an address and a password for a token pair. Every failure — unknown address, wrong password, unverified account — answers the same bodiless 401, and the unknown-address path spends the same hashing work as the others, so the response cannot be timed either.

get.description: Lists the caller's live sessions, newest first, each with the platform, device and app version that started it so a session can be recognised. No token and no digest is returned: the list exists to be read, not to be replayed.

post.description: Spends a refresh token exactly once and returns a rotated pair. Presenting an already-rotated token revokes the whole family and answers 401: that is the session-theft detector, and it answers exactly as an unknown or expired token does.

post.summary: Ask for a password reset link
post.description: Answers 202 for any address that is a valid address. Whether a mail follows is not stated and cannot be inferred from the response: a distinct answer here would tell an anonymous caller which addresses hold an account.

Spends the token from the reset mail exactly once, replaces the password and revokes every refresh token the account holds, so a password change ends every session opened with the old one. An access token issued moments earlier stays valid until it expires; that window is the 15 minutes the session design fixes. A 422 describes the new password only, never the token.

delete.description: Revokes the refresh-token family this access token belongs to, named by its sid claim, so no token from this session can be rotated again. The access token already issued stays valid until it expires — at most 15 minutes and 30 seconds — which is the accepted window in the threat register rather than an oversight.

Revokes one named session of the calling account. An unknown id, one already ended and one belonging to another account all answer 404, because a distinct answer would confirm that another account's session exists.

get.description: Returns every profile field with the visibility tier that governs it, plus the caller's music preferences. The owner is the one reader who sees every tier; what another user sees is projected per field, which is a different endpoint.

patch.description: Updates any subset of the profile. Each field carries its value and its visibility tier in the same object, so a field cannot exist without a tier — a value with no tier is 422, never a silent default to public. An absent field is left untouched; sending a null value with a tier clears it.

put.description: Replaces the whole preference set, genres and artists. Preferences are private to their owner and carry no visibility tier of their own. Both lists are bounded: an unbounded array behind an authenticated endpoint is unrestricted resource consumption.

get.description: Lists the caller's friends, newest first, paged. A friendship is symmetric: both parties see each other here, and neither can see it without the other.

delete.description: Ends the friendship for both sides at once, and clears the request rows between the pair so they may befriend again. Answers 404 when there is no friendship to end.

get.description: Lists pending requests in one direction: incoming are the ones addressed to the caller, outgoing the ones the caller sent. The direction is required, because the two screens that show these lists show one each.

post.description: Creates a pending request. Answers 409 when the pair are already friends, when a request is already pending in either direction, or when the caller asks themselves; 404 when no such account exists. A crossing request is not auto-accepted: nobody becomes a friend without accepting.

patch.summary: Accept or decline a friend request
patch.description: Only the recipient may answer. Accepting creates the friendship in the same transaction that marks the request accepted, so twenty simultaneous accepts produce one friendship. An unknown request, one already answered and one addressed to somebody else all answer 404.

delete.summary: Withdraw a friend request you sent
delete.description: Only the sender may withdraw; a recipient declines instead, which is a different verb and a different row state. The row is deleted rather than marked, so the pair may try again.

get.description: Matches a case-insensitive prefix of the display name, paged with a capped size. The display name is the only field searched: matching a profile field would let a stranger confirm a friends-only value by probing for it. A blank query returns nothing rather than everybody.

Returns the profile projected per field against the caller's relationship to its owner: self, friend or stranger. A field the caller may not see is absent from the body and is never read from the database, so a caller cannot tell a hidden field from an empty one. An account that does not exist answers the same sparse shape as one whose owner hid everything, so asking does not confirm existence.

post.description: The caller owns it. A playlist may be Everyone or InvitedOnly; LocationAndTimeRestricted is 422, because that licence belongs to an event and nothing checks a geofence on a playlist.

get.description: One scope at a time: mine, shared with me, or public. Paged with a capped size. A private playlist the caller is not named on never appears in any scope.
Returns the playlist with an ETag the client sends back as If-Match when it edits. A playlist the caller may not see answers 404, never 403, because 403 would confirm it exists.

patch.description: Requires If-Match carrying the ETag the client last read. A stale or absent token answers 412 and changes nothing: two clients editing at once is the failure this guard exists for.

delete.description: A soft delete, owner only: the row is stamped deleted and disappears from every read. Its audit trail keeps pointing at something that exists.

put.summary: Set a playlist's visibility and licence
put.description: Owner only: a collaborator who may edit the contents does not decide who may see them.

get.summary: List who is named on a playlist
get.description: Anybody who may see the playlist may see who is named on it. A caller who may not see the playlist answers 404, not an empty list, because an empty list would confirm it exists.

post.description: Owner only. 409 when they are already named, and when the owner names themselves — they already hold every right a collaborator grant could give.

delete.description: Owner only. 404 when there is no such grant on a playlist this caller owns.

get.summary: List a playlist's tracks in order
get.description: Anybody who may see the playlist may see its tracks. The response carries the ETag the client sends back as If-Match when it adds, moves or removes one. A caller who may not see the playlist answers 404, not an empty list, because an empty list would confirm it exists.

post.summary: Add a track to a playlist
post.description: Requires If-Match carrying the ETag of the track list the client last read. Appends by default; atHead or afterTrackId names a position. A playlist already holding its maximum number of tracks answers 409. The same video may appear twice: a playlist that plays a track twice is a playlist, not an error.

patch.summary: Move a track within a playlist
patch.description: Exactly one of afterTrackId or beforeTrackId. Requires If-Match: when two clients reorder the same list at once exactly one is applied and the other is told 412 and reloads, which is the whole point of versioning a collection.

delete.summary: Remove a track from a playlist
delete.description: Requires If-Match. Removing leaves the remaining order untouched: positions are sparse, so the hole costs nothing and no other row is rewritten.

post.description: The caller owns it. The window is two UTC instants and the end must be after the start. A LocationAndTimeRestricted licence must name the presence proof it requires, and a geofence proof must carry a centre and a radius, or the answer is 422.

get.description: One scope at a time: mine, the ones I was invited to, or public. Paged with a capped size. A private event the caller was not invited to appears in none of them.
Returns the event with an ETag the client sends back as If-Match when it edits. An event the caller may not see answers 404, never 403, because 403 would confirm it exists.

patch.description: Owner only, and requires If-Match carrying the ETag the client last read. A stale or absent token answers 412 and changes nothing.

delete.description: A soft delete, owner only: the row is stamped deleted and disappears from every read, so its audit trail keeps pointing at something that exists.

put.summary: Set an event's visibility, licence and presence policy
put.description: Owner only. The same rules creation applies: an event cannot become a LocationAndTimeRestricted event with nothing configured to check.

get.description: Owner only. Who else was invited to a private event is not a participant's business, and an empty list for a non-owner would still confirm the event exists — so the answer is 404.

post.description: Owner only. A duplicate is 409, decided by the unique index rather than by a read-then-write check. Inviting the owner is also 409: they already hold the strongest grant.

delete.description: Owner only. The gate is read live on every request, so the invitee loses access on their next call rather than on their next sign-in.

post.description: Any authenticated caller on a public event, an invitee on a private one. This is a roster and never a precondition: voting does not require it.

delete.description: `current` rather than a user id: the only attendance a caller may remove is their own.

canEdit.description: Whether they may write to it.
Whether they may write to it.
